## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Economy")]

[![Image 43](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d8/Sendai_Metropolitan_Employment_Area.svg/250px-Sendai_Metropolitan_Employment_Area.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sendai_Metropolitan_Employment_Area.svg)

Sendai [MEA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Employment_Area "Urban Employment Area")

Sendai is the center of the Tōhoku region's economy, and is the base of the region's logistics and transportation. The [GDP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDP "GDP") in Greater Sendai, Sendai [Metropolitan Employment Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_Employment_Area "Urban Employment Area") (1.6 million people), is US$61.7 billion in 2010.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-18) Sendai city by itself has a nominal GDP of approximately US$50 billion as of 2015[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-19) The city's economy heavily relies upon retail and services – the two industries provide approximately two thirds of the employment and close to half of the establishments.

Sendai is frequently called a branch-office economy[_[by whom?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Words\_to\_watch#Unsupported\_attributions "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Words to watch")_] because very few major companies are headquartered in the city. Various authorities are cooperating to alleviate this problem, primarily by encouraging high-tech ventures from [Tohoku University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tohoku_University "Tohoku University"), which is well known for its science and engineering departments. There are also incentives for startups available from the prefectural government.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-20)

[Tohoku Electric Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tohoku_Electric_Power "Tohoku Electric Power"), a major regional supplier of electric power, has its headquarters in Sendai and also operates the [Shin-Sendai Thermal Power Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shin-Sendai_Thermal_Power_Station "Shin-Sendai Thermal Power Station") located within the city.

Sendai's economic growth rate has stabilized since the 2011 Japan earthquake. The growth rate was only 0.4% in 2011 after the quake created economic turmoil in coastal areas. The year after, in 2012 the rate spiked to 10.4% after reconstruction efforts. It has since fallen to a closer trend to what is expected of 3.7% in 2013.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-:0-21)

Tourism in 2016 attracted an estimated 2.229 million visitors to Sendai.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-:0-21)

The city is served by [Sendai Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai_Airport "Sendai Airport") (located in neighboring [Natori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natori,_Miyagi "Natori, Miyagi")), which has international flights to several countries, and the Port of Sendai. ### Railway

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Railway")]

[JR East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JR_East "JR East")'s [Sendai Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai_Station_(Miyagi) "Sendai Station (Miyagi)") is the main transport hub for the city. The station is served by seven JR lines and is a major station on the [Tōhoku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C5%8Dhoku_Shinkansen "Tōhoku Shinkansen") and [Akita Shinkansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akita_Shinkansen "Akita Shinkansen") lines. An underground passage connects the station to the [Sendai Subway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai_Subway "Sendai Subway"). The subway has two lines— [Namboku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namboku_Line_(Sendai) "Namboku Line (Sendai)") ("north-south") and [Tōzai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T%C5%8Dzai_Line_(Sendai) "Tōzai Line (Sendai)") ("east-west") with a total of 30 stations. When completed in 2015, [Yagiyama station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yagiyama_Zoological_Park_Station "Yagiyama Zoological Park Station") became the highest-elevated subway station in the country, at 136.4 meters (448 ft).

The most well-known streets in Sendai, Jozenji-Dori (定禅寺通り) and Aoba-Dori (青葉通り), are both lined with [Japanese zelkovas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Zelkova "Japanese Zelkova"). These are symbols of "The City of Trees". Jozenji-Dori has a promenade and a few sculptures. It is a place of relaxation. Many events and festivals, such as the Sendai Pageant of Starlight and the Jozenji Street Jazz Festival, take place on Jozenji-Dori and in Kōtōdai Park (匂当台公園). Aoba-Dori is the main business road in Sendai. Other major roads in the city include Hirose-Dori ([ginkgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginkgo "Ginkgo")), and Higashi-Nibancho-Dori.

### Festivals

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Festivals")]

The most [famous festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_festivals "Japanese festivals") in Sendai is Tanabata, which attracts more than 2 million visitors every year and is the largest [Tanabata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanabata "Tanabata") Festival in Japan.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-25) It is relatively quiet compared to other traditional Japanese festivals, because its main attractions are intricate Tanabata decorations.

The Aoba Matsuri Festival follows more typical Japanese festival traditions, with a [mikoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikoshi "Mikoshi"), [floats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Float_(parade) "Float (parade)"), a samurai parade, and traditional dancing.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-26)

Local people burn their [New Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_New_Year "Japanese New Year") decorations and pray for health in the new year during the Dontosai Festival, the oldest festival in Miyagi Prefecture.

Various contemporary festivals also take place in Sendai, such as the Jōzenji Streetjazz Festival, the Michinoku Yosakoi Festival, and the Sendai Pageant of Starlight. The Jōzenji Streetjazz Festival is one of the largest amateur music festivals in Japan. It began as a jazz festival in 1991, but soon began to accept applications from all genres. The Michinoku Yosakoi festival is a dance festival, derived from the [Yosakoi Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yosakoi_Festival "Yosakoi Festival") that takes place in [Kōchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C5%8Dchi,_K%C5%8Dchi "Kōchi, Kōchi"). Trees in downtown Sendai are decorated with lights during the Sendai Pageant of Starlights. The event provided the idea for the Festival of Lights annually held in [Riverside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverside,_California "Riverside, California"), Sendai's sister city. In 2005, the streets were lit up with one million miniature bulbs.

### Specialties and crafts

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Specialties and crafts")]

[![Image 69](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Gyutan_teishoku.JPG/250px-Gyutan_teishoku.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gyutan_teishoku.JPG)

_[Gyūtan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C5%ABtan "Gyūtan")[teishoku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teishoku "Teishoku")_, a [table d'hôte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Table_d'h%C3%B4te "Table d'hôte") of beef tongue

Sendai is the origin of several foods, including _[gyūtan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gy%C5%ABtan "Gyūtan")_ (beef tongue, usually grilled), [hiyashi chūka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiyashi_ch%C5%ABka "Hiyashi chūka") (cold Chinese noodles), and [robatayaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robatayaki "Robatayaki") (Japanese-style barbecue). However, robatayaki was later introduced to [Kushiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kushiro,_Hokkaido "Kushiro, Hokkaido"), which developed and popularized the dish. As a result, many people believe Kushiro is the origin of Robatayaki. Zundamochi (ずんだ餅, [mochi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mochi "Mochi") balls with sweet, bright green edamame paste), and sasakamaboko (笹かまぼこ, [kamaboko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamaboko "Kamaboko") shaped like bamboo leaves) are also considered to be Sendai specialties. Sendai is also known for good [sashimi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sashimi "Sashimi"), [sushi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sushi "Sushi"), and [sake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sake "Sake"). This is because Sendai is near several major fishing ports, such as [Kesennuma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesennuma,_Miyagi "Kesennuma, Miyagi"), [Ishinomaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ishinomaki,_Miyagi "Ishinomaki, Miyagi"), and [Shiogama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiogama "Shiogama"), and the fact that Miyagi Prefecture is a major producer of [rice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rice "Rice"). There are many [ramen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramen "Ramen") restaurants in Sendai, and the area is known for a particular spicy [miso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miso "Miso")[ramen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramen "Ramen"). Also, Sendai station offers the most types of [ekiben](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ekiben "Ekiben") of any station in Japan. In autumn, many people organise Imonikai, a sort of picnic by the river which involves making a potato stew called _[Imoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imoni "Imoni")_. In winter, restaurants offer _seri-nabe_ (せり鍋), a regional specialty that consists of _[seri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oenanthe\_javanica#Japan "Oenanthe javanica")_ and various ingredients mixed in a hotpot.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-:1-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-31)

Many crafts from Sendai were originally created under the influence of the Date family during the [Edo period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edo_period "Edo period"). Examples are Sendai Hira, a hand woven silk fabric, Tsutsumiyaki pottery, and [Yanagiu Washi paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washi "Washi"). However, some crafts, such as umoregi zaiku (crafts created from fossil wood) were developed by low-ranking samurai who needed side jobs to survive. [Kokeshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokeshi "Kokeshi") dolls were popularized by hot spring resorts that sold them as gifts. Some relatively recent developments include Sendai Tsuishu [lacquerware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacquer "Lacquer") and Tamamushinuri lacquerware, both of which were developed after the [Meiji Restoration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiji_Restoration "Meiji Restoration").

Sendai was also known for its production of [Tansu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tansu "Tansu"), clothing drawers made from wood with elaborate ironwork.

Sendai is home to historical sites related to the [Date clan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Date_clan "Date clan"). The ruins of [Sendai Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai_Castle "Sendai Castle") are close to downtown on Aobayama, which also gives a panoramic view of the city. The [Zuihōden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuih%C5%8Dden "Zuihōden") is the tomb of [Date Masamune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Date_Masamune "Date Masamune") and is home to artifacts related to the Date family. It is on a hill called Kyogamine, which is the traditional resting place for Date family members. In [Aoba-ku](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aoba-ku,_Sendai "Aoba-ku, Sendai"), the [Ōsaki Hachimangū](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Csaki_Hachimang%C5%AB "Ōsaki Hachimangū")_shaden_, built in 1607 by Date Masamune, is designated a [National Treasure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Treasures_of_Japan "National Treasures of Japan"). [Mutsu Kokubun-ji Yakushidō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutsu_Kokubun-ji_Yakushid%C5%8D "Mutsu Kokubun-ji Yakushidō") is the [provincial temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provincial_temple "Provincial temple") of [Mutsu Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mutsu_Province "Mutsu Province").

Newer historical sites include the former home of [Doi Bansui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doi_Bansui?action=edit&redlink=1 "Doi Bansui (page does not exist)"), a famous lyricist, and a monument at Sendai City Museum that commemorates the Chinese writer [Lu Xun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu_Xun "Lu Xun"). Another statue of Lu Xun can be found in the Tohoku University Katahira Campus, where Lu Xun studied medical science. Older historical sites include the Tōmizuka Tomb, a tomb that dates back to the late 4th century or early 5th century, and the Tomizawa Preserved Forest site, where the excavated remains of a [Stone Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_Age "Stone Age") human settlement ([Upper Palaeolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Palaeolithic "Upper Palaeolithic") – roughly 20,000 years ago) have been protected by a large museum structure, built in 1996. The nearby [Site of Tagajō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Site_of_Tagaj%C5%8D "Site of Tagajō") was an important early fort and administrative centre.

Saikachi Gawa

Western Sendai is home to many sites of natural beauty, many of them found around Akiu Onsen and [Sakunami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sakunami "Sakunami"), which are [hot spring resorts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onsen "Onsen"). Sites around the Akiu area include the [Akiu Great Falls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akiu_Great_Falls "Akiu Great Falls"), sometimes counted as one of Japan's three great waterfalls, and the Rairai Gorge, known for its autumn colours. The Futakuchi Gorge contains waterfalls that have been designated as natural monuments and the Banji Cliffs, an example of [columnar basalt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basalt "Basalt").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-35)

The Sakunami area is also known for its natural environment, with [cherry blossoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherry_blossom "Cherry blossom") in the spring, and autumnal colours. The nearby Hōmei Shijuhachi Taki Falls is the name of waterfalls found in the higher reaches of the Hirose River. The origin of the name "Hōmei" (鳳鳴, "[Chinese phoenix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fenghuang "Fenghuang") cry") is said to come from ancient local inhabitants' claim that the sound of the waterfalls was similar to the legendary bird's call.

[Matsushima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsushima "Matsushima"), which is one of the [Three Views of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Views_of_Japan "Three Views of Japan"), is near Sendai, in [Matsushima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matsushima,_Miyagi "Matsushima, Miyagi").

### Shinto

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Shinto")]

Shinto shrines in Sendai include [Miyagiken Gokoku Shrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miyagiken_Gokoku_Shrine "Miyagiken Gokoku Shrine"), [Tsubonuma Hachiman Shrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsubonuma_Hachiman_Shrine "Tsubonuma Hachiman Shrine"), [Futahashira Shrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futahashira_Shrine "Futahashira Shrine"), and [Sendai Tōshōgū](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai_T%C5%8Dsh%C5%8Dg%C5%AB "Sendai Tōshōgū"), a memorial shrine of [Tokugawa Ieyasu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokugawa_Ieyasu "Tokugawa Ieyasu").

### Catholicism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Sendai&action=edit&section=31 "Edit section: Catholicism")]

The Catholic Church has been associated with Sendai since 1613, the year in which [Date Masamune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Date_Masamune "Date Masamune"), _daimyō_ of Sendai, built a galleon to send an [embassy to the Pope in Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_warship_San_Juan_Bautista "Japanese warship San Juan Bautista") headed by [Hasekura Tsunenaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasekura_Tsunenaga "Hasekura Tsunenaga").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sendai#cite_note-38) Although the embassy was successful in its aim of establishing relations with the Holy See, Masamune's plans were frustrated by the suppression of Christianity in Japan. The [Diocese of Sendai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Sendai "Diocese of Sendai") (previously the Diocese of Hakodate) was established in 1891, only two years after the promulgation of a new constitution guaranteeing freedom of religion in Japan, in 1889. The Bishop of Sendai currently oversees the four northern prefectures of Miyagi, Fukushima, Iwate and Aomori, serving 11,152 Catholics in 56 parishes. Mototerakoji, the Cathedral of the diocese, is located a few blocks north of Sendai Station.

## [7 Takeaways From Wrestlemania Weekend](link_1)

![Image 1](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1447.jpg?w=660)
Wrestlemania 42 is in the books and for the most part it will go down as a very disappointing weekend, highlighted by a few great moments but shadowed by a lot of bad and dissatisfaction. Night 1 of Mania 42 will go down as probably the worst Mania show I have ever seen, and Night 2 was in the mid to solid level show highlighted by a fantastic main event along with a fun ladder match. Here are my takeaways and thoughts regarding WWE’s biggest weekend of the year.

## 1. WWE cares more about the Mania in Wrestlemania

![Image 2](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1448.jpg?w=1024)
Across both nights, it was very clear to me that WWE doesn’t really care much about the in ring wrestling of their product. If they did, then there would’ve been more time for wrestling and the things we used to enjoy about wrestling like backstage interviews and video packages. Instead, across both nights, there was more time for ads, WWE promoting things, ads, celeberties in the crowd, ads, sponsorship plugs, and more ads. Instead, especially in Night 1, WWE focused on big entrances like the awful Liv Morgan entrance or even entrances like Randy Orton with him just slowly walking for 10 minutes to the ring, big moments like Paige returning and Bianca revealing she’s pregnant (congrats to her but why was this announcement on this show other than WWE just trying to make another moment for their big show), Speed hitting a splash on Logan Paul on ESPN2 to try and get some buzz, John Cena roboting his way through hosting Wrestlemania and other things that ate into time for matches that called for a good amount of time like Liv/Vaquer and Becky/AJ Lee. Even Night 2 had matches that could’ve went longer like Dom/Finn and Sami/Trick. It’s almost like WWE only cares about a couple matches getting enough time and to hell with the rest of the card because we need more time to plug Hulk Hogan’s documentary. The majority of both shows really hurt whatever investment I have left in WWE after some miserable months of TV and PLEs. If they focused more on actual wrestling, the weekend would’ve been more enjoyable.

## 2. Seth vs Gunther (And Bron Breakker) try to save Night 1

![Image 3](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1449.jpg?w=900)
The one good thing I can talk about with Night 1 was Seth/Gunther which was an incredible match. The start of the match just felt like a fight between two of the best in the world wanting to beat the other. Both guys worked hard and delivered a fantastic match that was so good I didn’t even care about the finish of the match which was Bron Breakker returning and costing Seth the match. At least the Bron interference is continuing the story between he and Seth, and it’s always good to see Bron because he’s just intense and comes off as different from anything else on these shows. Gunther is just an incredible heel wrestler who is physical and hard hitting and his style just meshed great with Seth who is just way better as a babyface fighting from underneath than as a heel. This match was a great 4.25 match and it really saved Night 1 from being a total disaster.

## 3. A Very Bizarre Night 1 Main Event

![Image 4](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1450.jpg?w=600)
Randy Orton vs Cody Rhodes at Wrestlemania 42 Night 1 was one of the most bizarre matches I have ever seen. First of all, the entrances and pre match took FOREVER and it was a drag waiting for the match to finally start. Pat McAfee being involved was always going to be terrible but at least they got the interaction with Pat and Jelly Roll out of the way and Pat was gone for the match (more on that later). Then, Randy Orton is selling his back and the commentary brings up “internet rumors” about Orton being hurt which is a play on the Dave Meltzer report a few days earlier. Why in the world are we even mentioning something that was in dirtsheets unless it was something that was fed to Meltzer which I could see. For most of the match, Randy Orton played babyface and Cody Rhodes played heel which is obviously not what the story was for the build of the match, but you know the fans are going to cheer Randy and probably boo Cody so I guess that makes sense. The pace of the match itself was very slow and methodical which is typical Randy Orton style match which usually isn’t very good especially in a big match setting like Wrestlemania. The blood in the match did help and as a match it was pretty good but in context it didn’t make any sense with the build of the match. Then we have a terrible ref bump where Orton gets poked in the eye in front of him and RKOs Charles Robinson who was BEHIND HIM! Then, the finish of the match happened which was Pat McAfee COMING BACK OUT IN A NECK BRACE AND REF SHIRT! WHY?? YOU HAD YOUR OUT WITH PAT BEFORE THE MATCH STARTED! Pat McAfee then, as the heel manager in a ref shirt, counts a NORMAL PIN FALL which Cody kicks out of. Then for some reason Orton RKOs McAfee which led to Cody hitting the Cross Rhodes and beating Orton. Then, RANDY ORTON ATTACKS CODY AND HITS THE PUNT TO END THE SHOW! ON WRESTLEMANIA! WE END WRESTLEMANIA WITH A HEAT ANGLE! And then there is a clip on WWE’s post show of Cody WALKING TO THE BACK AFTER BEING PUNTED IN THE HEAD! WHICH IS SUPPOSED TO BE THIS BIG MOVE THAT KNOCKS OUT EVERYONE! Just a bizzare and preposterous main event that some people I talked to tried defending but they fell on deaf ears because I can’t understand defending any of this. You can write Pat off with Jelly Roll fine, and then Cody just pins Orton clean in the middle of the ring. It is simple pro wrestling that worked for the other main event, so I don’t understand why we had to muddy the waters here on Night 1. This match and finish did nothing for anyone involved and I have no interest in Orton or Cody post Mania. If you were going to have Orton win the title just have him win with the punt, and if the Orton win is being saved for another show that doesn’t make much sense to me either. Just complete nonsense to end a very awful show.

## 4. Oba/Brock was simple pro wrestling

![Image 5](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1451.jpg?w=1024)
Oba vs Brock was to many people the most hyped match of the entire weekend and the only thing that mattered about this match was who won, which was the correct man. Oba is just white hot right now and it would’ve been a disaster if Brock won which I feared he would. The match itself was just simple pro wrestling that felt like a changing of the guard and a passing of the torch in a way with Brock not being able to stop the new, younger and stronger Oba who beat Brock in quick fashion. This match didn’t need to be a 5 star classic and it was never going to be, but this match needed to be Brock making Oba feel like an unstoppable force even for Brock who has been an unstoppable force for decades. It’ll be interesting to see what WWE does with Oba going forward as you know they will want to save him for big matches but who will they feud with in the meantime to keep him hot will be what I keep my eye on.

## 5. Brock Lesnar Retires (?)

![Image 6](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1452.jpg?w=686)
After Brock/Oba, Brock stayed on the mat for a long time which I think was good to sell how much impact Oba’s finisher is when it is keeping Brock Lesnar down for so long. Finally, Brock sits up and looks around, and then he takes his gloves and boots off which results in the crowd reacting (crowd was pretty terrible for much of the weekend by the way). Lesnar was emotional, something you very rarely see, Heyman was visbily emotional and it seemed he was out of character emotional rather than the theater emotional he sometimes acts like. Brock and Heyman then hug and Brock leaves the ring with his gloves and boots in the middle. This could always be a hint of a retirement with a set up to Gunther/Brock at Summerslam which ends up being Brock’s proper retirement. However, if this was Brock’s last match I think this is more impactful because Gunther has retired multiple people including JOHN CENA and has really gone nowhere in terms of where he was in the cards a year ago. Brock retiring after Oba soundly defeats him makes it all more impactful to me than a Gunther win would. Let’s just say this is the end for Brock Lesnar, I will try my best to remove all the out of the ring issues involving him but it’s hard to ignore all of that and it’s why I really haven’t cared about this Brock run for the past few months on top of his work just being very boring although he did look good tonight. Brock’s career is a pretty wild one when you look at it, his rise was so fast and then two years later he’s gone. Then, Brock pops up in the UFC and ends up being heavyweight champion there which no one could’ve saw coming. Brock then gets sick, retires from MMA and comes back to WWE and for the most part had a successful second run. Was it all great? No, there were several title runs Brock had that weren’t necessary and there were big show matches that didn’t deliver, but there was also great matches with John Cena, AJ Styles, Daniel Bryan, Roman Reigns and others that make the overall run worth it. I also think this current climate of WWE doesn’t need guys like Brock Lesnar anymore, or guys like John Cena. It’s time to start saying goodbye to WWE mainstays who are in their 40s and it’s time elevate guys like Oba Femi and Bron Breakker to spearhead the company’s future and beyond.

## 6. An Incredible Ladder Match

![Image 7](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1453.jpg?w=700)
Say what you want about modern day ladder matches, I still enjoy them and this ladder match was very enjoyable because you had 6 guys who wanted to make this match good and I thought they all delivered. This match was one of those matches where anyone could win and I’d be fine with it but I didn’t see a reason for Penta to lose the title right now as he’s over with the fans. Everyone looked good here and had good moments in the match, Dragon Lee, JD and Je’Von all shined with their high flying moves. Rey Mysterio turned back the clock in some ways, and even Rusev was a good base for the match. In the end though, Penta won and again I think it’s the right decision as Penta is a guy you can keep the IC belt on until you’re ready for him to move up the card. This match was a fun showcase match for 6 guys that delivered, incredible 4.25 match.

## 6. A Phenomenal Night 2 Main Event

![Image 8](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1454.jpg?w=640)
Roman Reigns vs CM Punk was simply phenomenal pro wrestling from the video package, to the entrances, to the match itself. CM Punk simply brings the best out of his opponents in the ring and he did it here with Roman who had does bring his best at Wrestlemanias year after year. These two just showed everyone why at their best they are better than everyone else, this match felt huge, it felt gritty and it felt like they were going to have to pull out everything to beat the other. The best thing I can say about this match is that there was no ref bump and there was no interference. Punk didn’t need to be kept strong here, this was about Roman beating him and taking his place back on the throne as the face of WWE (in his eyes). One of WWE’s best matches in a long time with two of their best all time performers. I wanted Punk to win, but if Roman could go back to having matches like that in this title run I’d be all for it. Only issues are I’m not sure how often we will be seeing Roman Reigns during this title run and who is he going to wrestle? It will also be interesting to compare Roman and Cody’s runs are as world champs as the two are basically just avoiding each other until one finally caves to job to the other which has been fascinating to watch behind the scenes. Overall, this Wrestlemania weekend wasn’t great but it was saved by Night 2 being solid enough to make it easier to forget the terrible Night 1. Hopefully tomorrow’s Raw will be a step in the right direction for WWE, only time will tell.

## [AustinonRasslin Star Ratings for 1/18-1/24](link_19)

![Image 9](https://411mania.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/WWE-Saturday-Nights-Main-Event-AJ-Styles-vs-Shinsuke-Nakamura-fist-bump.jpeg)
Another week in January down which means another week of star ratings with some really good standout matches this week!

![Image 10](https://www.f4wonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Titan-vs.-Komander.jpeg)
**Titan vs Komander CMLL Fin De Semana Internacional 1/18- 3.75**

Really fun lucha match here with two of the best and probably two of the most underrated luchadors going. Komander really stood out in this match, and I wish he’d get a bigger shine in AEW after seeing in matches like this. The crowd in the white hot Arena Mexico venue was also very into this match.

![Image 11](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G_CEYmHX0AAL_Ri.jpg)
**Bandido vs. Templario****CMLL Fin De Semana Internacional 1/18- 3.75**

This match started off really good, and then a fan ran in the ring and while the work in this match was good after they got the fan out of the ring, I really didn’t have as much interest in this match after that point. Plus, I am probably expecting way too much out of Bandido’s matches now after his amazing 2025. I’m expecting 4.5 star and above level matches almost every time now and that’s not fair but that’s my expectation. Still a fun match and Templario was good here too.

![Image 12](https://411mania.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/NJPW-Road-To-The-New-Beginning-1-19-26-645x370.png)
**Hartley Jackson, Ryohei Oiwa & Zack Sabre Jr. vs. Hirooki Goto, Oleg Boltin & YOSHI-HASHI NJPW Road to New Beginning 1/19- 4.25**

Very fun six man tag title match in a white hot Korauken Hall crowd and this crowd was really into this match. This match had high impact from the wrestlers and high energy from the crowd. I thought everyone did great in this match, maybe except Hartley Jackson who was in this match just to have fun big men spots with Oleg. The three that stood out to me though were Oleg Boltin, who I think is in like for a big push at some point, Hirooki Goto, who is picking up where he left off last year in terms of performance, and Ryohei Oiwa, who I think out of new blood that’s emerged in NJPW over the past few years is the guy people really need to pay attention to more than they are. The Goto/Oiwa interactions in this match were fantastic and I’m really excited for their singles match coming up next week. Great match that saw a title change which means we will get a rematch on the 11th which could mean another great match between these two teams.

![Image 13](https://www.njpw.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/0119_7.jpg)
**Shota Umino & Yuya Uemura vs. Taichi & Tomohiro Ishii NJPW Road to New Beginning 1/19- 4.5**

This tag match from the same show as the last match in Korakuen Hall felt like a make or break for Shota Umino, who has been constantly pushed but not accepted by the crowd. From the first few moments of this match, you knew that Taichi and Ishii were going to be the veterans that pushed Shota to his limit and he’d keep fighting and with his partner Yuya, they’d overcome the two hard hitting veterans and earn a tag title shot. All 4 were great in this match, but Shota’s performance really stood out to me. This match is long, 30 minutes, but there weren’t any moments in the match where I thought it was dragging. This will easily be a tag match I remember by years end, incredible stuff.

![Image 14](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dQUdMEt42qw/hq720.jpg?sqp=-oaymwEhCK4FEIIDSFryq4qpAxMIARUAAAAAGAElAADIQj0AgKJD&rs=AOn4CLDILAe87uBD1q011m6deRqeTK8GpA)
**CM Punk vs Finn Balor Raw 1/19- 4.25**

Some matches I really enjoy are between two veterans in their 40s, which was what this match was. I can’t remember a Finn Balor singles match this good, it’s definitely been a couple years, and Punk’s back to where he was in ring wise before the Seth feud really hindered him. The crowd in Ireland rooting for Finn increased the energy of the match as well as they were biting on Finn winning the title. Great match in front of a hot crowd.

## [7 Takeaways From Wrestlemania Weekend](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/04/20/7-takeaways-from-wrestlemania-weekend/)

![Image 1](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1447.jpg?w=660)
Wrestlemania 42 is in the books and for the most part it will go down as a very disappointing weekend, highlighted by a few great moments but shadowed by a lot of bad and dissatisfaction. Night 1 of Mania 42 will go down as probably the worst Mania show I have ever seen, and Night 2 was in the mid to solid level show highlighted by a fantastic main event along with a fun ladder match. Here are my takeaways and thoughts regarding WWE’s biggest weekend of the year.

## 1. WWE cares more about the Mania in Wrestlemania

![Image 2](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1448.jpg?w=1024)
Across both nights, it was very clear to me that WWE doesn’t really care much about the in ring wrestling of their product. If they did, then there would’ve been more time for wrestling and the things we used to enjoy about wrestling like backstage interviews and video packages. Instead, across both nights, there was more time for ads, WWE promoting things, ads, celeberties in the crowd, ads, sponsorship plugs, and more ads. Instead, especially in Night 1, WWE focused on big entrances like the awful Liv Morgan entrance or even entrances like Randy Orton with him just slowly walking for 10 minutes to the ring, big moments like Paige returning and Bianca revealing she’s pregnant (congrats to her but why was this announcement on this show other than WWE just trying to make another moment for their big show), Speed hitting a splash on Logan Paul on ESPN2 to try and get some buzz, John Cena roboting his way through hosting Wrestlemania and other things that ate into time for matches that called for a good amount of time like Liv/Vaquer and Becky/AJ Lee. Even Night 2 had matches that could’ve went longer like Dom/Finn and Sami/Trick. It’s almost like WWE only cares about a couple matches getting enough time and to hell with the rest of the card because we need more time to plug Hulk Hogan’s documentary. The majority of both shows really hurt whatever investment I have left in WWE after some miserable months of TV and PLEs. If they focused more on actual wrestling, the weekend would’ve been more enjoyable.

## 2. Seth vs Gunther (And Bron Breakker) try to save Night 1

![Image 3](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1449.jpg?w=900)
The one good thing I can talk about with Night 1 was Seth/Gunther which was an incredible match. The start of the match just felt like a fight between two of the best in the world wanting to beat the other. Both guys worked hard and delivered a fantastic match that was so good I didn’t even care about the finish of the match which was Bron Breakker returning and costing Seth the match. At least the Bron interference is continuing the story between he and Seth, and it’s always good to see Bron because he’s just intense and comes off as different from anything else on these shows. Gunther is just an incredible heel wrestler who is physical and hard hitting and his style just meshed great with Seth who is just way better as a babyface fighting from underneath than as a heel. This match was a great 4.25 match and it really saved Night 1 from being a total disaster.

## 3. A Very Bizarre Night 1 Main Event

![Image 4](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1450.jpg?w=600)
Randy Orton vs Cody Rhodes at Wrestlemania 42 Night 1 was one of the most bizarre matches I have ever seen. First of all, the entrances and pre match took FOREVER and it was a drag waiting for the match to finally start. Pat McAfee being involved was always going to be terrible but at least they got the interaction with Pat and Jelly Roll out of the way and Pat was gone for the match (more on that later). Then, Randy Orton is selling his back and the commentary brings up “internet rumors” about Orton being hurt which is a play on the Dave Meltzer report a few days earlier. Why in the world are we even mentioning something that was in dirtsheets unless it was something that was fed to Meltzer which I could see. For most of the match, Randy Orton played babyface and Cody Rhodes played heel which is obviously not what the story was for the build of the match, but you know the fans are going to cheer Randy and probably boo Cody so I guess that makes sense. The pace of the match itself was very slow and methodical which is typical Randy Orton style match which usually isn’t very good especially in a big match setting like Wrestlemania. The blood in the match did help and as a match it was pretty good but in context it didn’t make any sense with the build of the match. Then we have a terrible ref bump where Orton gets poked in the eye in front of him and RKOs Charles Robinson who was BEHIND HIM! Then, the finish of the match happened which was Pat McAfee COMING BACK OUT IN A NECK BRACE AND REF SHIRT! WHY?? YOU HAD YOUR OUT WITH PAT BEFORE THE MATCH STARTED! Pat McAfee then, as the heel manager in a ref shirt, counts a NORMAL PIN FALL which Cody kicks out of. Then for some reason Orton RKOs McAfee which led to Cody hitting the Cross Rhodes and beating Orton. Then, RANDY ORTON ATTACKS CODY AND HITS THE PUNT TO END THE SHOW! ON WRESTLEMANIA! WE END WRESTLEMANIA WITH A HEAT ANGLE! And then there is a clip on WWE’s post show of Cody WALKING TO THE BACK AFTER BEING PUNTED IN THE HEAD! WHICH IS SUPPOSED TO BE THIS BIG MOVE THAT KNOCKS OUT EVERYONE! Just a bizzare and preposterous main event that some people I talked to tried defending but they fell on deaf ears because I can’t understand defending any of this. You can write Pat off with Jelly Roll fine, and then Cody just pins Orton clean in the middle of the ring. It is simple pro wrestling that worked for the other main event, so I don’t understand why we had to muddy the waters here on Night 1. This match and finish did nothing for anyone involved and I have no interest in Orton or Cody post Mania. If you were going to have Orton win the title just have him win with the punt, and if the Orton win is being saved for another show that doesn’t make much sense to me either. Just complete nonsense to end a very awful show.

## 4. Oba/Brock was simple pro wrestling

![Image 5](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1451.jpg?w=1024)
Oba vs Brock was to many people the most hyped match of the entire weekend and the only thing that mattered about this match was who won, which was the correct man. Oba is just white hot right now and it would’ve been a disaster if Brock won which I feared he would. The match itself was just simple pro wrestling that felt like a changing of the guard and a passing of the torch in a way with Brock not being able to stop the new, younger and stronger Oba who beat Brock in quick fashion. This match didn’t need to be a 5 star classic and it was never going to be, but this match needed to be Brock making Oba feel like an unstoppable force even for Brock who has been an unstoppable force for decades. It’ll be interesting to see what WWE does with Oba going forward as you know they will want to save him for big matches but who will they feud with in the meantime to keep him hot will be what I keep my eye on.

## 5. Brock Lesnar Retires (?)

![Image 6](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1452.jpg?w=686)
After Brock/Oba, Brock stayed on the mat for a long time which I think was good to sell how much impact Oba’s finisher is when it is keeping Brock Lesnar down for so long. Finally, Brock sits up and looks around, and then he takes his gloves and boots off which results in the crowd reacting (crowd was pretty terrible for much of the weekend by the way). Lesnar was emotional, something you very rarely see, Heyman was visbily emotional and it seemed he was out of character emotional rather than the theater emotional he sometimes acts like. Brock and Heyman then hug and Brock leaves the ring with his gloves and boots in the middle. This could always be a hint of a retirement with a set up to Gunther/Brock at Summerslam which ends up being Brock’s proper retirement. However, if this was Brock’s last match I think this is more impactful because Gunther has retired multiple people including JOHN CENA and has really gone nowhere in terms of where he was in the cards a year ago. Brock retiring after Oba soundly defeats him makes it all more impactful to me than a Gunther win would. Let’s just say this is the end for Brock Lesnar, I will try my best to remove all the out of the ring issues involving him but it’s hard to ignore all of that and it’s why I really haven’t cared about this Brock run for the past few months on top of his work just being very boring although he did look good tonight. Brock’s career is a pretty wild one when you look at it, his rise was so fast and then two years later he’s gone. Then, Brock pops up in the UFC and ends up being heavyweight champion there which no one could’ve saw coming. Brock then gets sick, retires from MMA and comes back to WWE and for the most part had a successful second run. Was it all great? No, there were several title runs Brock had that weren’t necessary and there were big show matches that didn’t deliver, but there was also great matches with John Cena, AJ Styles, Daniel Bryan, Roman Reigns and others that make the overall run worth it. I also think this current climate of WWE doesn’t need guys like Brock Lesnar anymore, or guys like John Cena. It’s time to start saying goodbye to WWE mainstays who are in their 40s and it’s time elevate guys like Oba Femi and Bron Breakker to spearhead the company’s future and beyond.

## 6. An Incredible Ladder Match

![Image 7](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1453.jpg?w=700)
Say what you want about modern day ladder matches, I still enjoy them and this ladder match was very enjoyable because you had 6 guys who wanted to make this match good and I thought they all delivered. This match was one of those matches where anyone could win and I’d be fine with it but I didn’t see a reason for Penta to lose the title right now as he’s over with the fans. Everyone looked good here and had good moments in the match, Dragon Lee, JD and Je’Von all shined with their high flying moves. Rey Mysterio turned back the clock in some ways, and even Rusev was a good base for the match. In the end though, Penta won and again I think it’s the right decision as Penta is a guy you can keep the IC belt on until you’re ready for him to move up the card. This match was a fun showcase match for 6 guys that delivered, incredible 4.25 match.

## 6. A Phenomenal Night 2 Main Event

![Image 8](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/img_1454.jpg?w=640)
Roman Reigns vs CM Punk was simply phenomenal pro wrestling from the video package, to the entrances, to the match itself. CM Punk simply brings the best out of his opponents in the ring and he did it here with Roman who had does bring his best at Wrestlemanias year after year. These two just showed everyone why at their best they are better than everyone else, this match felt huge, it felt gritty and it felt like they were going to have to pull out everything to beat the other. The best thing I can say about this match is that there was no ref bump and there was no interference. Punk didn’t need to be kept strong here, this was about Roman beating him and taking his place back on the throne as the face of WWE (in his eyes). One of WWE’s best matches in a long time with two of their best all time performers. I wanted Punk to win, but if Roman could go back to having matches like that in this title run I’d be all for it. Only issues are I’m not sure how often we will be seeing Roman Reigns during this title run and who is he going to wrestle? It will also be interesting to compare Roman and Cody’s runs are as world champs as the two are basically just avoiding each other until one finally caves to job to the other which has been fascinating to watch behind the scenes. Overall, this Wrestlemania weekend wasn’t great but it was saved by Night 2 being solid enough to make it easier to forget the terrible Night 1. Hopefully tomorrow’s Raw will be a step in the right direction for WWE, only time will tell.

## [AustinonRasslin Star Ratings for 1/18-1/24](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/01/26/austinonrasslin-star-ratings-for-1-18-1-24/)

![Image 9](https://411mania.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/WWE-Saturday-Nights-Main-Event-AJ-Styles-vs-Shinsuke-Nakamura-fist-bump.jpeg)
Another week in January down which means another week of star ratings with some really good standout matches this week!

![Image 10](https://www.f4wonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Titan-vs.-Komander.jpeg)
**Titan vs Komander CMLL Fin De Semana Internacional 1/18- 3.75**

Really fun lucha match here with two of the best and probably two of the most underrated luchadors going. Komander really stood out in this match, and I wish he’d get a bigger shine in AEW after seeing in matches like this. The crowd in the white hot Arena Mexico venue was also very into this match.

![Image 11](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G_CEYmHX0AAL_Ri.jpg)
**Bandido vs. Templario****CMLL Fin De Semana Internacional 1/18- 3.75**

This match started off really good, and then a fan ran in the ring and while the work in this match was good after they got the fan out of the ring, I really didn’t have as much interest in this match after that point. Plus, I am probably expecting way too much out of Bandido’s matches now after his amazing 2025. I’m expecting 4.5 star and above level matches almost every time now and that’s not fair but that’s my expectation. Still a fun match and Templario was good here too.

![Image 12](https://411mania.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/NJPW-Road-To-The-New-Beginning-1-19-26-645x370.png)
**Hartley Jackson, Ryohei Oiwa & Zack Sabre Jr. vs. Hirooki Goto, Oleg Boltin & YOSHI-HASHI NJPW Road to New Beginning 1/19- 4.25**

Very fun six man tag title match in a white hot Korauken Hall crowd and this crowd was really into this match. This match had high impact from the wrestlers and high energy from the crowd. I thought everyone did great in this match, maybe except Hartley Jackson who was in this match just to have fun big men spots with Oleg. The three that stood out to me though were Oleg Boltin, who I think is in like for a big push at some point, Hirooki Goto, who is picking up where he left off last year in terms of performance, and Ryohei Oiwa, who I think out of new blood that’s emerged in NJPW over the past few years is the guy people really need to pay attention to more than they are. The Goto/Oiwa interactions in this match were fantastic and I’m really excited for their singles match coming up next week. Great match that saw a title change which means we will get a rematch on the 11th which could mean another great match between these two teams.

![Image 13](https://www.njpw.co.jp/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/0119_7.jpg)
**Shota Umino & Yuya Uemura vs. Taichi & Tomohiro Ishii NJPW Road to New Beginning 1/19- 4.5**

This tag match from the same show as the last match in Korakuen Hall felt like a make or break for Shota Umino, who has been constantly pushed but not accepted by the crowd. From the first few moments of this match, you knew that Taichi and Ishii were going to be the veterans that pushed Shota to his limit and he’d keep fighting and with his partner Yuya, they’d overcome the two hard hitting veterans and earn a tag title shot. All 4 were great in this match, but Shota’s performance really stood out to me. This match is long, 30 minutes, but there weren’t any moments in the match where I thought it was dragging. This will easily be a tag match I remember by years end, incredible stuff.

![Image 14](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/dQUdMEt42qw/hq720.jpg?sqp=-oaymwEhCK4FEIIDSFryq4qpAxMIARUAAAAAGAElAADIQj0AgKJD&rs=AOn4CLDILAe87uBD1q011m6deRqeTK8GpA)
**CM Punk vs Finn Balor Raw 1/19- 4.25**

Some matches I really enjoy are between two veterans in their 40s, which was what this match was. I can’t remember a Finn Balor singles match this good, it’s definitely been a couple years, and Punk’s back to where he was in ring wise before the Seth feud really hindered him. The crowd in Ireland rooting for Finn increased the energy of the match as well as they were biting on Finn winning the title. Great match in front of a hot crowd.

![Image 15](https://www.wwe.com/f/styles/wwe_16_9_xl/public/2026/01/20260113_NXT_Match_SeanEli_16x9_tonight.jpg)
**Sean Legacy vs Eli Knight NXT 1/20- 3.75**

NXT’s men’s division is one of the worst rosters I have ever seen, but it still has some good wrestlers like these two who had a great, high flying match in the PC. Sean Legacy has been around for a while, and we talked about him a couple of weeks ago so we know he’s good. Eli Knight has came out of nowhere and has already caught my attention, I’d love to see him vs Je’Von Evans at some point down the line. Really fun stuff in this match.

![Image 16](https://www.pwtorch.com/site/wp-content/uploads/post/2026/01/G-vw_yaawAAfVMY-678x381.jpg)
**Fallon Henley & Lainey Reid vs. Kendal Grey & Wren Sinclair vs. Sol Ruca & Zaria NXT 1/20- 4.5**

While the men’s division in NXT is pretty dire, the women’s division is incredible. This match was great and the PC crowd were really into it and all 6 women had moments to shine, but three women stood out for me. Sol Ruca, who I think has potential to be a top women’s star, Kendal Grey, another women’s star in the making, and Lainey Reid who really impressed me in this match as I don’t watch a lot of Fatal Influence stuff, but she was really good in this match and gave a really great Blue Thunder Bomb in this match. This match was a sign that if given the right booking, women’s wrestling in WWE/NXT can really be great. My one nitpick is whatever they’re doing with this ZaRuca storyline as I can’t stand the tag team that isn’t getting along but are still teaming storyline.

![Image 17](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G_OW7R0a0AAnkoz.jpg)
**Konami vs Rina Stardom New Year Stars 2026 In Korakuen Hall 1/21- 4.5**

I mostly loved this match for Rina and her performance in front of a hot Korakuen Hall crowd. The only thing about this match I wasn’t crazy about was Konami as I’ve never been the biggest fan of her work, but she was a good opponent for Rina here and the match was still really good, definitely recommend seeing it.

![Image 18](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/G_WncIEWMAAC4zf.jpg)
**Speedball Mike Bailey vs. Samoa Joe AEW Dynamite 1/21- 3**

The in ring work from these two were good, especially from Speedball, but the constant run ins from The Opps really hurt my enjoyment of this match. Constant run ins is a problem in all of wrestling and this is just one example. Still a solid match though.

[![Image 19](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/wp-content/uploads/G-7AMrIXQAAbS8M.jpg)](https://dknetwork.draftkings.com/wp-content/uploads/G-7AMrIXQAAbS8M.jpg)

**Daniel Garcia, Jon Moxley & Wheeler Yuta vs. Hechicero, Lance Archer & Rocky Romero Street Fight AEW Dynamite 1/21- 3.5**

Really fun street fight here, Lance Archer is my MVP in this match because when was the last time he even wrestled in AEW and he shows up here and has a great performance, especially against Moxley. Jon Moxley is also one of the best hardcore wrestlers of all time so anytime he’s in a match like this you know it’s going to be fun, excellent stuff.

![Image 20](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image.png?w=959)
**Josh Alexander vs. Kenny Omega AEW Dynamite 1/21- 3.75**

Kenny Omega isn’t quite back at his form this time last year, but he’s slowly getting there I think. Omega’s confidence is slowly coming back to him and having an opponent like Josh Alexander helps. This felt like a mix of old school and modern wrestling and it resulted in a fun match between the two. I’m still waiting for that really good Omega match though, but it might be when Omega wrestles MJF later this year.

![Image 21](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-1.png?w=959)
**Swerve Strickland vs Kevin Knight AEW Dynamite 1/21- 4.25**

Swerve’s best match in months is against Kevin Knight who continues to impress and continues to show me why he should be a singles guy moving forward. There was high impact moments and high flying moments that made this match great. The finishing stretch of this match was also great, really hope we see more from these two down the line.

![Image 22](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-2.png?w=686)
**Carmelo Hayes vs. Ilja Dragunov Smackdown 1/23- 4**

Another really good performance from Carmelo Hayes this month, this time in a rematch with Iija Dragunov. This match wasn’t good as their match from last month, and I’m kind of getting tired of Iija talking so much during matches, but the work here was still good. The Miz run in at the end sucked and I wish he’d get off my TV forever, but you know they’re doing a Miz/Melo match so we’ll see how that goes. I expect another Melo/Iija match at some point as well and that’ll probably be very good.

![Image 23](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-3.png?w=640)
**Komomo Minami vs. Victoria Yuzuki MARIGOLD 1/24- 3.5**

This match went to a 15 minute time limit draw which felt needless, but then again they’re trying to elevate Minami by having her go to the limit with a current champion in the company. Victoria Yuzuki really impressed me at times in this match, and Minami was solid but you can tell both of these women are still green and have a lot to improve on.

![Image 24](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-5.png?w=645)
**Mayu Iwatani vs. Utami Hayashishita MARIGOLD 1/24- 4**

This match was for the GHC Women’s Title, but this match and whole show was a celebration on Mayu Iwatani’s 15th anniversary of becoming a pro wrestler. We had a pre match ceremony with special guests coming out and interacting with Mayu, which were great and I wish American wrestling just took more things from Japanese wrestling but then again maybe not because it wouldn’t be as good. After the ceremony, Utami comes out and the match starts and Mayu goes from being so happy and emotional to deadly serious and takes the fight right to Utami. Mayu was incredible in this match, whereas Utami was fine but she’s not where she used to be five years ago where she was having incredible matches with Syuri. A really good match and a great performance from Mayu here who got the win on her anniversary.

![Image 25](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-6.png?w=1024)
**IYO SKY & Rhea Ripley vs. Liv Morgan & Roxanne Perez Saturday Night’s Main Event 1/24- 4**

Really fun tag match, especially towards the end. All four of these women are great and I think Liv Morgan might be a better tag wrestler than singles. The run in with Raquel didn’t really bother me as it was to continue the feud with her and Stephanie Vaquer who came out and attacked her. There were some really hard hitting kicks in this match as well and the crowd was into it. Another thing I enjoyed from this match was there wasn’t any in fighting with any of the teams and there was a clean finish as well. Really good match.

![Image 26](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-7.png?w=1024)
**AJ Styles vs. Shinsuke Nakamura Saturday Night’s Main Event 1/24- 4.75**

An amazing turn back the clock performance from Shinsuke Nakamura here as he went all out for someone he respects in AJ Styles, who is nearing retirement. AJ Styles is in my top 5 all time, and he can still go which makes it kind of sad he’s about to retire, but Nakamura really showed signs of his prior peak days. Shinsuke didn’t have the bodysuit on in this match, he looked more serious and he took it to AJ in this match. Crowd was into it, hard hitting strikes and a great finish at the end. Amazing match and I can’t wait to see AJ’s last match with Gunther as sad as it is that he’s retiring.

![Image 27](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/image-8.png?w=784)
**Damian Priest vs. Randy Orton vs. Sami Zayn vs. Trick Williams****Saturday Night’s Main Event 1/24- 3.5**

It was going to be diffcult for this match to top the rest of this show as this show was WWE’s best show in months, but the Montreal crowd wanted Sami Zayn to win to earn a WWE title shot, and they were hot for Orton as well, so that all helped this match. The Orton/Sami interactions were great in this match and they were by far the two best performers in this match. Trick Williams has incredible charisma but I’m not sure if he’ll ever have the in ring skills to match it, but he fit in to this match as well as he could. Damian Priest was also in this match, and he handled his role in the match well.

## [AustinonRasslin Star Ratings From 1/11/26-1/17/26](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/01/19/austinonrasslin-star-ratings-from-1-11-26-1-17-26/)

Another week, another batch of star ratings for select matches I either found to be interesting to give my rating whether good or bad. Let’s take a look at the good, the bad, and the ugly from this week.

Last Week’s Star Ratings: [https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/01/12/austinonrasslin-star-ratings-from-1-1-26-1-9-26/](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/01/12/austinonrasslin-star-ratings-from-1-1-26-1-9-26/)

![Image 28](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8981.jpg?w=396)
**AMAKUSA vs. Daiki Odashima NOAH Legacy Rise 1/11/26:****4.25****stars**

A very fun junior style match in Korakuen Hall between two top juniors in NOAH. AMAKUSA makes his second appearance in back to back weeks this time against young, rising star Daiki Odashima who is absolutely destined to become a star in a few years. This was a great match in front of a great crowd and I’m excited to see more from Odashima.

![Image 29](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8982.jpg?w=250)
**Masa Kitamiya vs. Yoshiki Inamura NOAH Legacy Rise 1/11/26: 4 stars**

A 28 minute main event with these two wouldn’t have been what I’d done here, but it was still entertaining even with the Team 2000X run ins. Kitamiya is very good and I think he’s underused by NOAH for a long time now, Inamura has also been a guy underused by NOAH and now finally getting a big GHC title run that was elevated by this match. This match overall was a nice hoss battle between two former tag partners where Inamura won in the end to redeem the title. The crowd in Korakuen helped the match too.

![Image 30](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8983.jpg?w=1024)
**Chihiro Hashimoto vs. Saya Iida Sendai Girls 1/11/26: 3.75 stars**

Didn’t like this as much as others did, there was a lot of this match that felt slow and repetitive. There were a lot of moments in this match with chops and strikes and it felt like it was just for the sake of doing them rather than using it for the story of the match. This match was meant to be a hoss battle between two joshi wrestlers and the match improved towards the end with a wild suplex bump, but overall I can’t give it anything in the 4s.

![Image 31](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8984.jpg?w=1024)
**Hazuki vs. Mei Seira****STARDOM 1/11: 4.5 stars**

Incredible match here in Korakuen Hall, Hazuki has been one of the best women’s wrestlers in the world that I wish I could see more of because she was amazing in this match. Mei Seira is someone I’ll keep an eye out for more as well, very strong performance from her. This match was a hard hitting sprint in front of a hot crowd that had a struggle and that had two women giving it all they had until one won the match. Very good match and I’d be down to see a rematch down the line.

![Image 32](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8985.jpg?w=728)
**Fukigen Death, Konami & Rina vs. Hina, Lady C & Tomoka Inaba STARDOM 1/11: 4 stars**

Despite this match having wrestlers I’m just not crazy about, this was a fun Korakuen Hall main event match. Rina especially was the star coming out of this match to me, as she’s someone that has been on my radar over the past year and will continue to be. Her sister, Hina, also shined in this match and you can tell when the two sisters interacted in this match that there is magic with them, great chemistry between them and money to be made in a big match with those two down the line. Very fun tag match.

![Image 33](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8986.jpg?w=645)
**Mayu Iwatani & Victoria Yuzuki vs. Miku Aono & Utami Hayashishita MARIGOLD 1/12/26: 3.5 stars**

I appreciate the effort these 4 gave, but this match was waaaaaaaaaaay too long for a preview tag setting up big title matches later in the month in a Korakuen Hall that only had 700 people in the building. 28 minute match where 20 of those minutes felt long, boring and honestly a but self indulgent. The finish was good but they could’ve gotten a lot more out of a solid, 15 minute main event match in my opinion.

![Image 34](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8987.jpg?w=1024)
**AJ Styles vs. Gunther Raw 1/12- 3.75 stars**

Another match where I thought the first few minutes were kind of slow, but they picked it up and had a great second half of the match with the story of Styles wanting to tap Gunther out…and he techically did just when the referee didn’t see it. I know people are going to have different feelings about the finish of this match, but I loved it. I think the ending of Gunther taking advantage of the ref not seeing him tap out, AJ losing it at the ref thinking he won, only to turn around and get low blowed and lose the match, It’s a great way to get HEAT on Gunther because as much as the commentary want to act like Gunther has heat right now after retiring John Cena, it doesn’t really feel like it and it doesn’t matter how much piped in noise you put in the arenas. The crowd in Germany weren’t going to really boo Gunther that hard anyway, so we didn’t have to worry about fake noise in this one. Anyway, a great heelish win for Gunther and this means we get a rematch at some point, maybe AJ’s retirement match.

![Image 35](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8988.jpg?w=768)
**Darby Allin vs PAC AEW Dynamite: Maximum Carnage 1/14/26: 4.25****stars**

I LOVED this match! The brawling in the crowd, THAT suplex spot on the steps, PAC just dominating Darby and Darby bumping like he usually does, PAC tweaking his ankle and Darby going right for it. Really, REALLY good stuff. This match was so good even the run ins didn’t bother me, because unlike at Full Gear, Darby got one over on the Death Riders and defeated PAC. These two have amazing chemistry and I need a third match at Revolution, make it 2/3 falls.

![Image 36](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8989.jpg?w=739)
**Bishop Kaun & Toa Liona vs. Jake Doyle & Mark Davis vs. Kevin Knight & Mike Bailey vs. Young Bucks****AEW Dynamite: Maximum Carnage 1/14/26: 3.5****stars**

A solid, PWG style tag match that was a bit sloppy at times but still good. JetSpeed once again shined, GOA continue to improve, the Bucks were pretty much the team keeping everything in place, and Doyle and Davis I thought were incredible. I am kind of upset they’re just going to lose to FTR right off the bat, but hopefully the match is still good.

![Image 37](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8990.jpg?w=1024)
**Bandido vs. MJF AEW Dynamite: Maximum Carnage 1/14/26: 4.25****stars**

MJF’s character has become fatigued for my taste, but his in ring work is still very good and he meshed well with Bandido here in this match. The story of this match was very simple, Bandido is beloved and MJF is hated. Bandido is the high flying babyface, and MJF is the cheating heel that is trying to keep Bandido grounded. You put all of that together and this is the match you get and it was great, MJF pulls out the win but Bandido didn’t lose anything in losing this match. Maybe one day Bandido will become world champion in AEW, but it wasn’t on this night.

![Image 38](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8991.jpg?w=739)
**Frankie Kazarian vs. Mike Santana TNA Impact 1/15/26: 2.5 stars**

TNA’s debut on AMC was one of the worst wrestling shows I have ever seen headlined by this world title main event. A match that actually started out pretty good that I couldn’t wait for it to be over by the end. A ref bump that happened by Santana just walking over to the ref in a middle of a back and forth and Kazarian bumping into both of them, then overbooked kickout spots and overbooked finisher spots. In the end, Santana won but my goodness it felt like it took to get to that point, especially watching this entire show that was AWFUL! To make things worse, these two had a rematch at the Genesis PPV, which we will get to shortly!

![Image 39](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8992.jpg?w=640)
**Carmelo Hayes vs. Leon Slater Smackdown 1/16/26: 4 stars**

Another very good match from Carmelo here, this time with TNA rising star Leon Slater, who is probably very close to being WWE bound. This match was in England, so the crowd was supporting Leon huge here and it was a very fun match between two high flyers. Carmelo is getting back into his old NXT groove in my opinion, and Leon Slater has been one of my favorites to watch over the past year. Carmelo wins with a cutter off the top because his leg has been targetted all match and he knew he couldn’t hit the leg drop off the top like he usually would, very good match.

![Image 40](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8993.jpg?w=686)
**Ilja Dragunov vs. Sami Zayn Smackdown 1/16/26: 4 stars**

The rematch from these two’s US Title match wasn’t as good as the first, but I still enjoyed this gritty fight these two had. I thought Sami was excellent here, he was punching Iija so hard that Iija started bleeding which helped the match in my opinion. Sami was pretty excellent in this match, while I am kind of losing interest in Iija since he’s returned. Iija has started making more of these weird noises and talking to his opponent more during his matches when like dude just wrestle the match, and the German Suplex segment of his matches take FOREVER for him to finish, brother you are not Kurt Angle. Iija is still really good I don’t want anyone thinking I dislike him, there are just some things I’d change about his matches. Anyway, really solid match here.

![Image 41](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8994.jpg?w=1024)
**Blue Panther vs. Ultimo Guerrero CMLL 1/16- 3.5 stars**

OLD MAN BATTLE! Ultimo is in his 50s and Panther in his 60s, and these two were doing moves that guys in their 20s and 30s do. Incredible stuff from two lucha libre legends, and Blue Panther’s renaissance run the past few years has been amazing to watch.

![Image 42](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8995.jpg?w=1024)
**Ricochet vs Titan CMLL 1/16- 3.75 stars**

I’m really happy that Ricochet is getting back to having good matches again, something happened around the summer that caused Ricochet to kind of be stuck in limbo and wrestling the Hurt Syndicate for months in decent matches, but you knew Ricochet could be doing better things. This match with CMLL’s Titan is an example of those better things, a very fun Arena Mexico main event with two high flyers. Ricochet’s heel work here was great and it still amazes me how great he is as a heel.

![Image 43](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8996.jpg?w=1024)
**Mara Sade vs. Ryan Nemeth TNA Genesis- DUD**

Awful, awful match, and none of it is Sade’s fault as she is still green and she followed the veteran’s lead here. The problem is the veteran is one of the worst wrestlers I ever seen, Ryan Nemeth, which boggles my mind considering his brother used to be a really good wrestler. They did a typical intergender match where the guy doesn’t take the woman seriously, but then it got really weird. Nemeth started telling Sade “I know you love me” and weird stuff like that, it’s 2026 what the hell are we doing? Then, Ryan starts gyrating in Sade’s face, my brother this is not the Attitude Era. To top it all off, Nemeth cheated and won the match! This could’ve been a *maybe* a star had Sade won the match, but having the heel do all this weird stuff to the woman babyface, AND have him cheat, AND have him win?? Awful, awful match. A very heavy favorite for worst match of the year and it was only 5 minutes long. DUD!

![Image 44](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8997.jpg?w=1024)
**The Hardys vs The Righteous TNA Genesis 2026- 1 star**

This match sucked too, but I give it a star because I felt bad for Jeff Hardy here. The old man Hardys had to try and make this match with the Righteous somewhat good, but for some reason they decided to a Bray Wyatt/Karrion Kross level lore match and it sucked. The work was slow from the Righteous having way too much heat on the Hardys, to the Hardys just moving slow in general. The finish of this match sucked too with The Righteous just letting the Hardys win proclaiming they want to feel pain instead of winning the titles, very stupid stuff.

![Image 45](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8998.jpg?w=678)
**Frankie Kazarian vs. Mike Santana Texas Death Match (Special Referee: Nic Nemeth) TNA Genesis 2026: 2.5**

I will say, TNA did use the OG Texas Death Match rules instead of the rules AEW uses, which I think are the better rules. You pin the guy first, then they have 10 seconds to beat the count or lose the match. That being said, this match wasn’t going to be that good regardless of the rules they used. The beginning of this match was a walk and brawl through the crowd, not a fight, just walking around and hitting each other every few seconds. Both of these guys did try when they got to the ring, but nothing really felt interesting. Plus, the finishing stretch was overbooked, the cutter off the top through a table, a splash off the ladder through a table that Kazarian kicked out of, before finally Santana wins the match off of a spinning clothesline with his arm wrapped in barbed wire. I thought the best guy in this match was actually Nemeth’s referee work, and they actually saved him getting involved physically until after the match which I liked.
