## [AustinonRasslin Star Ratings from 1/1/26-1/9/26:](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2026/01/12/austinonrasslin-star-ratings-from-1-1-26-1-9-26/)

Hopefully this will be a consistent thing I do, but I will be issuing star ratings every week. Now the matches I rate will only be the matches I have watched in the given time frame. There may be matches on shows I skip over, or shows I skip over entirely. I’m only interested in ratings matches I am interested in, for the most part. This first star ratings issue will be from wrestling shows that happened between 1/1/26 and 1/9/26.

![Image 46](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8842-1.jpg?w=1024)
**AMAKUSA vs. Hiromu Takahashi NOAH The New Year 1/1/2026- 4.25 stars**

NOAH’s first show of the year was apparently really bad aside from this match, and it makes sense because Hiromu’s NOAH run over the past few months has been fun. This match took a little while for it to get me interested, but once they hooked me I was locked in. AMAKUSA always has been underrated in my opinion and he’s still really good at 40 years old. Hiromu seemingly cares more in these NOAH matches than in his NJPW matches nowadays and it showed in this match. Takahashi played the heel role in this match as he’s the outsider who has the company’s belt, defending against an underdog like opponent in AMAKUSA, and in the end, the underdog won and upset Hiromu in a fantastic match. AMAKUSA was doing stuff I’ve never seen before especially at the end when he hit a beautiful splash on Hiromu to win the GHC Junior Heavyweight Championship.

![Image 47](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8843-1.jpg?w=968)
**MIRAI vs. Sareee Tochi Pro Happy New Year & Shinjiro Otani Aid ~ Stand Up Again And Again 1/1/2026- 4 stars**

Sareee has been my Women’s Wrestler of the Year the past two years, and it’s matches like this that make her that. Sareee is just really good at her style of wrestling, she hits hard, she’s serious and it’s that seriousness that brings out this aura about her. MIRAI is also really good, I just haven’t seen a lot of her lately because she’s in a company that isn’t all that interesting. She did look good here in a match with one of the best in the world, and the match told a really good story of MIRAI hanging with a veteran before getting caught in the end and Sareee winning the match. I’d love to see this match again down the line.

![Image 48](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8844-1.jpg?w=640)
**Carmelo Hayes vs. Johnny Gargano Smackdown 1/2/26- 4 stars**

The US Title matches over the past few months have been the one thing that is consistently interesting on WWE TV where a lot of things in that product aren’t. Sami Zayn and Iija Dragunov had fun title runs, now it’s Carmelo Hayes’s turn and in this match he wrestled Johnny Gargano, who he’s been kinda feuding with lately. Gargano isn’t as good as his peak, and he’s a heel in this match where I think he’s a better babyface, and he was also wearing a t shirt for half the match which threw me off. Despite all that, this was a solid match that had great action from both guys mixed in with Candice LeRae doing good heel manager work at ringside trying to help her husband win the US Title. Carmelo is continuing to look more like what we thought he’d be when we saw him in NXT, his performances are improving and the crowd is supporting him and they were with Melo during the finishing stretch of the match. If Carmelo has more matches like this, we’ll be seeing him more on these star rating issues throughout the year.

![Image 49](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8845-1.jpg?w=299)
**Mayu Iwatani vs. Takumi Iroha MARIGOLD First Dream 1/3/26- 4.25 stars**

This GHC Women’s Title Match was really good and had some hard hitting action, but there were some nitpicks. For one thing, the match was a little too long, 25 minutes in the co main event when the main event was going about the same length kinda hindered the match for me. Mayu Iwantani was great here and proved why she is one of the best women’s wrestlers of all time, and Takumi has been great the past few years as well. The story of this match was great with these two off and on feuding since the beginning of their careers, and Mayu having to pull out everything in her moveset to win the title. There was the botched hurricanrana spot Mayu went for but I think she was able to pull off selling the fact that she was just exhausted as the spot was towards the end of the match.

![Image 50](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8846.jpg?w=1024)
**Mai Sakurai vs. Miku Aono MARIGOLD First Dream 1/3/26- 3.75**

I appreciate the effort from both ladies here, but this 26 minute main event match didn’t really do a whole lot for me. While they did have some intense moments, this match was just too long in my opinion. In the middle of the match, the two Joshi wrestlers did this spot on a table where the two stand on the table and start hitting each other. Only problem was you can clearly see the table giving out the moment both women are on the table, and it continues to break through as they fight. They finally do a piledriver spot on this already bent table and that spot possibly rang Miku’s bell because she seemed off for the rest of the match, but they were able to get through it. It’s definitely a match that could’ve been better.

![Image 51](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8847.jpg?w=724)
**Arisu Endo vs. MIRAI TJPW Tokyo Joshi Pro ’26 1/4/26- 4**

Really good match between a TJPW mainstay and a MARIGOLD mainstay, and another really good performance from MIRAI. This match was hard hitting and intense which is what great Japanese wrestling usually is. MIRAI especially was throwing some really crazy strikes at Endo, and she got the title win as the outsider which makes things interesting for MIRAI moving forward in TJPW.

![Image 52](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8849.jpg?w=1024)
**Miu Watanabe vs. Suzume TJPW Tokyo Joshi Pro ’26 1/4/26- 5**

The first 5 star match of the year, in my opinion, goes to Miu Watanabe and Suzume for an incredible match. Suzume was doing things in this match I’ve never seen before, and Miu has continued to improve in the ring. One of Miu’s big move is a giant swing and Suzume did a great job of countering the move. Suzume kept bringing the fight to Miu forcing Miu to hit Suzume with an alternate version of her finish to win the match and retain her title. Exceptional, hard hitting match with innovative moves and a very invested crowd. It’s one of those matches where you have to watch it to really appreciate it, definitely a MOTY candidate for sure.

![Image 53](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8850.jpg?w=600)
**Saya Kamitani vs. Syuri Wrestle Kingdom 20- 3.75**

A quick sprint between two of the top stars in Stardom in the Tokyo Dome, it was a really cool moment and fun match but if you watched this you knew these two could have a better match with more time. Syuri winning the title for title match did surprise me as I thought they’d give Saya a big moment in the dome.

![Image 54](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8365.jpg?w=664)
**Aaron Wolf vs EVIL Wrestle Kingdom 20- 3.75**

Now for this match, a 3.75 is actually a really good success! The thing about EVIL’s matches is there is constant interference from his House of Torture stablemates that helps him win matches. With this match however, it worked because the good guy was able to prevail in the end. Now as for Aaron Wolf, he looked promising and has a lot of potential, and the fans LOVE him as he received a huge pop from nearly 50,000 people in the Tokyo Dome. Wolf coming out shedding the usual judo outfit and revealing his shaved head and traditional young boy in ring look of black trunks and black boots was a great touch as well. Some people have made comments about Wolf’s physique but we have a ton of wrestlers that are in great shape, being back the tubby looking fat wrestlers who can still kick ass. Aaron Wolf is a gold medal winner who has a legit judo background and could definitely kick ass in a real fight, so it’s fine with me. This was a great first match for Wolf and I am excited to see more from him this year.

![Image 55](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8852.jpg?w=1024)
**Konosuke Takeshita vs. Yota Tsuji Wrestle Kingdom 20- 4.75**

Winner take all match for the Global and World titles in NJPW. This match took a while to get going for me personally, but after the first 10 of so minutes I finally got invested in the match. Takeshita was my WOTY for 2025 and he’s been one of my favorites to watch for a few years now, and Yota is great too and I think he is going to be an outstanding face for NJPW this year. These two had a hard hitting match, they did each other’s moves, and the crowd in the Tokyo Dome was really into it especially towards the end of the match. The finish of the match is what really got this rating for me personally, as I was skeptical of Yota winning the titles and becoming the top guy. Not only did Yota win but also Yota won with the traditional move of a NJPW young lion, the Boston Crab submission forcing Takeshita, an outsider of the company, to submit to the hold. Fantastic storytelling and a great finish to a great match.

![Image 56](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8853.jpg?w=645)
**Hiroshi Tanahashi vs. Kazuchika Okada Wrestle Kingdom 20- 5**

I won’t say this is a perfect wrestling match, but I do think this is a perfect retirement match. You can make the argument that Hiroshi Tanahashi is the greatest wrestler of all time, especially for Japanese wrestling and for NJPW. This match was a perfect sendoff for the Ace and he faced off against perhaps his biggest rival, Kazuchika Okada who was making a return match to Japan since signing with AEW. I know everything about this match and show is about Tanahashi, but Okada was fantastic here. I’ve liked Okada’s AEW run in 2025, it was better than 2024, however, there is something about Okada in the Tokyo Dome that just feels perfect. This setting is where the Rainmaker really thrives and he thrived in this match even if he was doing some of his AEW bits in this match, it still worked because Okada is great at being a dickhead heel wrestler. Okada played a great foil to the worn down, retiring Tanahashi who continued to fight with everything he could until Okada finally put him down with one last Rainmaker. This may not be the best match these two have had, but it also could be. Either way, as a retirement match, it’s the perfect way for the Ace to say goodbye.

![Image 57](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8854.jpg?w=1024)
**OSKAR & Yuto-Ice vs. Ryohei Oiwa & Zack Sabre Jr. New Year Dash 1/5/2026- 4.5**

I love really good tag team wrestling, and that is what this match was. You have the two technical experts against the two powerhouses and it was a great combination for a great match. The real story here was between Oiwa and Yuto-Ice who have known each other since their Young Lion days and you can tell there’s bad blood/jealously there, which I love. Yuto and Oiwa are going to be big stars moving forward for the company as the crowd was into both guys throughout the match. Sabre looked great, and OSKAR looked good too, he’s much better in a tag team right now.

![Image 58](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8855.jpg?w=825)
**Asuka & Kairi Sane vs. IYO SKY & Rhea Ripley Raw 1/5/26- 3.5**  
(Yes, I watched all of Raw for some reason, hopefully I won’t do that again)

You can tell these four knew that they were going to have to go through two ad breaks before getting to the last segment of the match, so that’s why this match really didn’t get going until then. The work was still good and the finish was good too, solid performances all around here.

![Image 59](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8856.jpg?w=900)
**Becky Lynch vs. Maxxine Dupri Raw 1/5/26- 1**

Awful, just an awful match. Maxxien Dupri has had no business in the position she has been in. She had no reason being a champion, and she had no reason wrestling Becky Lynch who as great as she used to be is currently having her worst run ever in my opinion. Despite that, I was feeling bad for Becky as she had to work a match with Maxxine who was so slow and didn’t meet her marks. I know Becky is a generous worker and wanted to make a star out of a Maxxine like she’s done in the past with some women, but this was never going to work and it didn’t work. The finish to this match was also awful as the intention was for Becky to sneak away with the win but the result didn’t feel that way as it felt like Maxxine just watched herself get pinned. Bad, bad stuff here. No more Maxxine Dupri wrestling for the love of God, I don’t even know if she’d do well on EVOLVE.

![Image 60](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8857.jpg?w=399)
**Liv Morgan vs. Lyra Valkyria Raw 1/5/26- 2.75**

I wanted this match to be better because I’m a fan of both women, but this really didn’t do a whole lot for me and I thought the finish sucked. The typical Judgement Day interference added with this stupid Bayley gimmick they continue to do ruined the match for me.

![Image 61](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8858.jpg?w=576)
**Bron Breakker vs. CM Punk Raw 1/5/26- 4.25**

This was a long match, 26 minutes, and in the end I feel like the wrong man won as this was the perfect time to go with Bron Breakker, but I still enjoyed the match. The run ins between the Vision and Mysterio/Penta/Dragon Lee were fine and didn’t ruin the match for me. The botched rana spot was a blow to the match though, and I’m not sure what Punk was thinking but he also didn’t look like he was all there by the end of the match so he may have had his bell rung at some point. Bron Breakker looked like an absolute star here doing these wild movements that no one else does in the ring (can’t wait for someone to tell him to tone it down which will ruin his aura). Again, I thought the wrong guy won but the match was still great and at the very least they are probably doing a rematch down the line.

![Image 62](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8859.jpg?w=399)
**Jackson Drake vs. Sean Legacy EVOLVE 1/7/26- 3.75**

No I did not watch NXT, but I did watch this EVOLVE title match between Jackson Drake and Sean Leagcy. I’ll be honest, I know nothing about Jackson Drake and he comes across as very bland while Sean Legacy has been great for years now. These two did work hard even though it felt like there were 25 people in whatever room this show is held in. The commentary also held the match back for me as Rosenberg and Robert Stone are two of the worst personalities in all of wrestling right now (Bring back Robbie E). The finishing stretch of the match was also really well done.

![Image 63](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8860.jpg?w=1024)
**The Demand vs Jack Perry and The Young Bucks Dynamite 1/7/26- 4.25**

I thought this match was fantastic, PWG style action that only these guys could do. I’ve been wishy washy on the Bucks for years now, but I think their work over the past few years has been amazing and I think it’ll continue this year now that they’re back as babyfaces after being heels for a couple of years. Their moves may come across as too “choreographed” but I still enjoy them. I also thought Jack Perry was great in this match as he continues to improve over the past few weeks. Ricochet has been a fantastic heel in AEW and I’m glad he’s getting more of a chance to show how much of a great wrestler he still is. The Gates of Agony were terrific in this match as well, please give me more of these two in matches like this, they fit perfectly in matches with this style.

![Image 64](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8861.jpg?w=1024)
**Carmelo Hayes vs. Shinsuke Nakamura Smackdown 1/9/26- 3.75**

Another solid US Title match from Carmelo Hayes here this time with Shinsuke Nakamura. Nakamura is a long ways away from his prime, but he did a real good job of beating the crap out of Melo, forcing to champ to bounce back and eventually win. Carmelo’s selling in this match, I thought, was really good as well. Things are looking up for Hayes and I just hope it means bigger and better things for him moving forward.

![Image 65](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8862.jpg?w=686)
**Cody Rhodes vs Drew McIntyre 3 Stages of Hell Smackdown 1/9/26- 3.75**

I watched this match 3 times before I settled on this rating, while I enjoyed the work of the first two falls, something fell apart during the cage match. I’m not sure if they were stalling for time or what but something just wasn’t clicking in the 3rd stage of the match. At one point, these two were just punching each other back and forth for what seemed like forever, and then we get to the finish which wasn’t good either. Jacob Fatu comes back and attacks Drew first, before attacking Cody leaving the door open for Drew to sneak out of the cage and win the WWE title. Not a good 3rd stage, poorly formatted finish, and a title win that I feel like is too little too late for McIntyre who is probably going to lose the title in a couple of months anyway.

![Image 66](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/img_8863.png?w=1024)
**Barbaro Cavernario vs. Mistico CMLL 1/9/26- 4.5**

Perfect, old school lucha libre wrestling here. You had the heel Barbaro and his goons at ringside doing whatever he could to win the title from Mistico and Mistico once again defying the odds and winning in front of his fans that in Arena Mexico that love him so much. It’s a perfect formula that shows why CMLL is so hot right now and will probably continue to be hot. Barbaro has always had a cool factor to him and was good in this match, but Mistico once again stole the show with his selling and his ability to get the crowd to root him on to victory. Excellent match.

## [Best of the Super Juniors 32 Preview: Matches to Watch](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2025/05/08/best-of-the-super-juniors-32-preview-matches-to-watch/)

![Image 67](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3164-1.jpg?w=600)
One of my favorite tournaments in pro wrestling is here once again, the Best of Super Juniors 32! This year’s lineup has mostly the usual lineup, with a few intriguing newcomers. I’m going to break down every show on this tour by going through the matches you should go out of your way to see for the next few weeks.

## Night 1: May 10th

![Image 68](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3151-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 1 kicks off with a mix of A and B Block action in Chiba, and there’s 3 matches that I think will be worth watching. Hiromu Takahashi vs KUSHIDA may not be the matches they had years ago, but they’ll still deliver a quality match. Kosei Fujita vs Francesco Akira has a chance to be really good, and the main event of El Desperado vs Titan could be a banger as Desperado is once again having a sneaky good in ring year. The one negative I have from this show is debuting Nick Wayne in NJPW against Sho…this should be in the middle of the tournament. This first night could be better but it’s a good start.

## Night 2: May 11th

![Image 69](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3152-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 2 is a worse lineup than Night 1 in my opinion, but there are still 2 matches I’d keep my eye on for this show: Ninja Mack vs Robbie X and Kevin Knight vs DDT’s MAO. Those two matches could be show stealers for sure. Wato/Connors and YOH/Eagles I’m not completely sold on. The main event of this show is Ryusuke Taguchi vs Taiji Ishimori would be great 10 years ago, but not in 2025.

## Night 3: May 14th

![Image 70](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3153-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 3 we’re in the historic Korakuen Hall and we have a full show of BOSJ action. There’s 7 matches I’d recommend on this show, and so far this looks like the show of the whole tournament. Here are the matches I’d recommend for May 14th:

Ninja Mack vs Francisco Akira

Kevin Knight vs Robbie Eagles

Kushida vs Robbie X

MAO vs Taiji Ishimori (Ishimori might be washed to some people, but I think he picks and chooses his spots, this could be one of them.)

YOH vs SHO (I know I know, I get it, but it’s in Korauken Hall and with this history these two have and the crowd behind them, maybe this could be good? I’m hoping)

El Desperado vs Nick Wayne (Huge test for Nick Wayne here, this’ll make or break his tournament for me-and I expect him to hit it out of the park)

Night 3 Main Event: Hiromu Takahashi vs Kosei Fujita (Speaking of big tests, this is a big test for both guys here to me. Kosei is main eventing against a top star, and Hiromu needs to prove he’s still got it after a few months of just kinda floating around)

## Night 4: May 15th

![Image 71](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3154-1.jpg?w=600)
We’re back in Korakuen Hall the next night for another loaded night of action, and while it’s not as good as Night 4 there’s still 5 matches I’d circle for this card.

Kushida vs Ninja Mack

Robbie Eagles vs Nick Wayne

Titan vs MAO

El Desperado vs Taiji Ishimori

Night 4 Main Event: Hiromu Takahashi vs Francesco Akira (Big spot for Akira)

## Night 5: May 17th

![Image 72](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3155-1.jpg?w=600)
Another night of loaded BOSJ action and this is another contender for show of the tournament in my opinion. There’s six matches on this card that I would recommend:

Clark Connors vs Robbie X (Interfaction match so this’ll either be fun or boring, no way around it)

Titan vs Taiji Ishimori

Kushida vs Kosei Fujita

Kevin Knight vs Nick Wayne (A match that might be so good Tony Khan is going to book it on a random Collision this summer)

Co Main Event: Hiromu Takahashi vs Dragon Dia

Night 5 Main Event: El Desperado vs MAO (Could be match of the tournament)

## Night 6: May 18th

![Image 73](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3156-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 6 is kind of a weak card, only 4 matches I see as worth it:

Kevin Knight vs Titan

Kosei Fujita vs Robbie X

Robbie Eagles vs Taiji Ishimori

Night 6 Main Event: Hiromu Takahashi vs Clark Connors (Connors can deliver in big spots, and this a perfect spot for him to shine)

## Night 7: May 20th

![Image 74](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3157-1.jpg?w=600)
This may be a reach from me, but I honestly think this is a sneaky good card with 4 out of the 5 matches that can deliver:

Ninja Mack vs Hiromu Takahashi

Kosei vs Yoshinobu Kanemaru (Kanemaru can have a good technical match with Kosei if he chooses to)

Kushida vs Clark Connors

Night 7 Main Event: Master Wato vs Robbie X (Not sure why this is the main event, I guess this was meant to be Wato/Bushi before Bushi quit the company to follow Tetsuya Naito. Maybe this’ll be good and motivate Wato to have a good match. I haven’t watched a whole lot of Wato since his return from injury so I’m not sure how he’ll do this tournament)

## Night 8: May 22nd

![Image 75](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3158-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 8 has 3 matches I see as worth it as the B Block headlines the Edion Arena in Osaka:

Titan vs Robbie Eagles

Nick Wayne vs Taiji Ishimori

Night 8 Main Event: El Desperado vs YOH (Hopefully Despy can get a good main event out of YOH)

## Night 9: May 24th

![Image 76](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3159-1.jpg?w=600)
Night 9 is another night with both blocks having matches, and there’s 6 matches on this show I’d recommend:

Ninja Mack vs Clark Connors

Francesco Akira vs Robbie X

Eagles vs MAO

Knight vs Ishimori

Hiromu vs Kanemaru (These two had a fun match on a Dontaku show a couple of years ago, so I’m going this’ll be the same, or maybe it goes 45 seconds who knows)

Night 9 Main Event: El Desperado vs Ryusuke Taguchi (Another Taguchi main event for some reason, maybe he’ll try against Despy)

## Night 10: May 25th

![Image 77](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3160-1.jpg?w=600)
The last night double block action is on this show and there’s 5 matches I’d go out of my way to see:

MAO vs Nick Wayne

Ninja Mack vs Kosei Fujita

Francesco Akira vs Clark Connors

El Desperado vs Kevin Knight

Night 10 Main Event: Master Wato vs Hiromu Takahashi (Main Event Wato, hopefully he delivers)

## Night 11: May 27th

![Image 78](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3161-1.jpg?w=600)
A Block finals happen on May 27th, we don’t know yet what the match order will be but I have 3 matches to look for:

Kosei Fujita vs Clark Connors

Hiromu Takahashi vs Robbie X

Kushida vs Francesco Akira

## Night 12: May 29th

![Image 79](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3162-1.jpg?w=600)
The final night of B Block happens on the 29th and it’s one of the weakest shows of the tournament with only Wayne/Titan and Despy/Eagles being the only interesting matches on this card. This worries me on who will be in contention for the finals.

## Finals Predictions

The finals for the Best of the Super Juniors will be on June 1st and this year it’s the winner of A Block vs the winner of B Block. So who has the best chances of making it to the finals and winning the tournament? Let’s break it down:

A Block:

No Shot at All:

Ninja Mack, Dragon Dia, Robbie X, Kanemaru, & Kushida: There’s no chance any of these we guys have a shot in making the finals and I’ll be shocked if it happened.

Take a Chance:

Francisco Akira & Clark Connors: These are two guys I’ve been high on for a while and while I don’t think they’ll be in the finals, if you wanted to swing for the fences on two guys one of these two would be good picks, but this year isn’t either of their years.

Master Wato: Two Time Winner?

You may have forgotten that Master Wato actually won the BOSJ in 2023, and then hasn’t done a lot since due to injury. Maybe they want to go back to the well with Wato, he might be in the finals but I doubt he wins the tournament.

A Five-Peat?:

Hiromu Takahashi has won the BOSJ 4 times, 3 in a row, and hasn’t won since 2022. Maybe he’s due? Maybe NJPW wants to go back with Hiromu as the top junior now that Tetsuya Naito is gone? Clearly either they don’t want him to go heavyweight or Hiromu simply doesn’t want to or it would’ve happened by now. I could absolutely see Hiromu in the finals, since he hasn’t even been in the finals since 2022, but I don’t think he should win the tournament.

My A Block Winner: Kosei Fujita

In a time in NJPW where they’ve been focusing on the young guys heavily, Kosei Fujita is a junior who is ready to take the top spot. He had a great title match against El Desperado earlier this year and he just lost the junior tag titles so this seems like it’s the right time to elevate Fujita into that spot. I think Kosei/Connors on the 27th could be a match to determine who makes it to the Finals, with Kosei advancing to the Finals. Now does he win the trophy…well that depends…

B Block:

No Shot at All:

Taguchi: There’s no way…there’s just no way

Outsiders:

MAO, Kevin Knight, Nick Wayne, Titan: These guys all work for other companies so while it would be fun to see these three in the finals against Kosei I doubt it.

The Champion:

El Desperado is the reigning champion in this tournament and I highly doubt he’s even in the finals let alone wins the whole tournament.

Don’t Think Gedo Won’t Do It:

Ishimori, SHO, YOH: Some of these three have been to the finals before, Ishimori last year. I don’t think these 3 would be good choices though, and they definitely shouldn’t win the tournament. You can’t count out the chances of it happening though, we never know what’s truly going through Gedo’s mind

My B Block Winner: Robbie Eagles

Robbie Eagles is a guy that’s been a hard worker for the company for years, he had some title runs during the pandemic and he’s just someone that’s always good in the ring. I think Eagles making the finals and facing his tag team partner, Fujita, would be a good story and make for a great BOSJ finals…so who wins???

MY BOSJ 32 WINNER:

I think Kosei Fujita will be the one to win the Best of the Super Juniors this year, he’s ready for it and I think he’s earned the spot. Overall, I hope it’s a fun tournament this year and can’t wait to follow it!

## [My Thoughts on the WWE Departures](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2025/05/05/my-thoughts-on-the-wwe-departures/)

It’s that time of the year again, WWE is cutting costs and getting rid of talent, which is what they did this past Friday. I’m gonna break down these departures one by one, what they did in the company, what they’ve could’ve done, and what their futures will be.

![Image 80](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3282-1.jpg?w=1024)
Dakota Kai: This one probably hits me the most because I’ve always been a big fan of Dakota Kai, now presumably going by King Kota. Kota was let go a few years ago, but then was brought back for Bayley’s Damage Control stable. Dakota was a consistent player on TVs until her injury in 2023, she came back and after a while she just wasn’t as much of a focal point on the TVs as she could’ve been. This year alone she was in the finals for the women’s IC title and a few months later she’s gone. Doesn’t make any sense to me but, a few of these do not make sense to me. As for her future, it seems as King Kota will do just fine as I could see her working for several companies. I’m not sure about AEW because they had a chance before to sign her and never did, but who knows, I think Kota would be great in AEW.

![Image 81](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3283-1.jpg?w=1024)
Shayna Baszler: Another woman I’ve always liked, and someone WWE had always started and stopped with ever since she debuted on the main roster. Shayna could’ve been a dominant champ on the main roster just like in NXT, but I have a theory that after a while Triple H sees some of his former NXT Black and Gold signings as “good hands” that can get other talent over (DIY for example). Shayna is another wrestler in this group I could see in pretty much any company as she’s got a different look about her than most female wrestlers and is still a good wrestler despite being in her mid 40s.

![Image 82](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3284.jpg?w=1024)
Braun Strowman: This guy gets fired, comes back, breaks his neck, comes back from that, and is fired about a year later. Braun was someone that I still enjoyed seeing because there’s not a lot of giants in wrestling anymore and I love watching the giants. Sure, he might be physically regressed but I still think someone like Braun on your roster is good to have. Braun was a key part in helping guys like Bronson Reed and Jacob Fatu get over, and you need a guy like Braun on your roster who is credible enough to be in feuds with guys you wanna get over. As for his future, Braun didn’t really do much during his last hiatus from WWE so I’m not sure what he’ll do this go around.

![Image 83](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3285.jpg?w=1024)
Kayden Carter & Katana Chance: Keep these two from cutting promos (especially Katana) and these two could’ve been a credible team on the main roster. Yes they won tag titles but no one really remembers that. As for their future, maybe they’ll end up somewhere but I’m not sure about AEW. I’d love to see them somewhere like TJPW or Stardom and see how they do.

![Image 84](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3286-1.png?w=645)
Gigi Dolin: Another woman I really liked and have always liked since before WWE, after the Toxic Attraction split, Gigi seemed to be off and on in terms of pushes in NXT (sorry I don’t really watch NXT like that, I can’t imagine watching that week to week). As for her future, Priscilla Kelly could end up in several companies just like Dakota and Shayna. I think Gigi has a chance to do good stuff post WWE despite coming off some injuries.

![Image 85](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3287-1.jpg?w=1024)
Cora Jade: This one is probably the headliner of all the departures and I’m surprised about this one. Despite Cora being not that great in the ring and character wise since returning from injury, she’s someone that’s always been consistently booked well in NXT and I always thought a call out was imminent but it didn’t happen. In terms of her future, I’m sure Elyana Black will get several bookings but I’m not sure how she’s gonna do in ring. Black may be too far gone drinking the WWE Style Koolaid that she just keeps that with her wherever she goes, I’ll hope for the best though.

![Image 86](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3288-1.jpg?w=1024)
Eddy Thorpe: This is another one I found a little surprising because it seemed like Shawn Michaels loved the guy. He’s got a pretty good look, but that’s probably about it. As for his future, I’m not sure if we’ll see Karl Fredericks back in NJPW after a nasty exit with the company, but I could see him pop up in NOAH or AJPW. Karl could also end up staying in America and working there as well.

![Image 87](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3289.jpg?w=1024)
Jakara Jackson: I wasn’t really a fan of her work in NXT, but her and Lash Legend seemed to get over well for the WWE audience, but they clearly see Lash as the star. I’m not sure where Jakara goes from here, I don’t think she’s a good fit in AEW or even ROH, I’d say TNA maybe but who knows if they’ll even be allowed to sign these releases/departures.

![Image 88](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3290-1.jpg?w=696)
Shotzi: Technically, Shotzi isn’t gone from the company at the moment but might as well be. Shotzi was always someone I thought could be a babyface star, despite some injuries. Once Shotzi got called up and Vince decided to turn her heel for no reason, it was pretty much wraps for Shotzi after that sadly. Shotzi is once again another woman that I could see wrestle pretty much everywhere and I hope she does.

![Image 89](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/img_3291-1.jpg?w=870)
Riley Osbourne, Joe Coffey, Mark Coffey, Wolfgang, Javier Bernal, Dani Palmer: I wish all of these wrestlers the best, but honestly I had no interest in watching them so I don’t have anything to say about what they did or where they’ll go from here. However, I will say firing Riley Osbourne when he was injured and rehabbing is pretty awful, but it’s sadly not something WWE has never done. Gallus will absolutely end up somewhere I know that, they can be good hands pretty much anywhere.

Lastly, news like this always sucks and it will always suck. I can’t imagine defending a wrestling company ever, but especially in this case and especially WWE. We know this is their playbook, and it’s worse now that they’re owned by TKO. It’s releases that are always done but they came at a pretty bad time considering there is a lack of interest in the TV product at the moment. I hope everyone that got released is able to thrive in wrestling going forward if they choose to do so.

## [Wrestlemania 41 Weekend Takeaways](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/2025/04/21/wrestlemania-41-weekend-takeaways/)

![Image 90](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2990.jpg?w=1024)
Wrestlemania 41 has come and gone, with a week and a weekend full of things to talk about both positive and negative. Here are a few things I took away from the biggest wrestling weekend of the year.

## 1. Stand & Deliver Highlights

![Image 91](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2943.jpg?w=1024)
I want to touch on NXT Stand & Deliver briefly. I did enjoy Stand & Deliver for the most part. My favorite matches were Fraxiom vs Hank & Tank (4.5/5), the Women’s North American Title Ladder Match (4), the Four Way for the Women’s Title (4), and the main event triple threat match for the NXT Title (4.75) which was the match of the night and a potential best match of the weekend for WWE. We all know NXT isn’t the NXT of years ago, but their big shows when done right I still enjoy and they still have some good talent in NXT that I would like to see on the main roster very soon, and hopefully we’ll see some of that talent in the coming weeks.

## 2. WWE buys AAA

![Image 92](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2944.jpg?w=1024)
In one of the biggest and most shocking stories for me this weekend, WWE announced on their countdown show on Saturday they have acquired the lucha libre wrestling organization known as AAA. I have a lot of thoughts on this, for one, I’m a sucker for “wrestling company being bought” news because when WCW was bought by WWF, I was only 4 years old and have no memory of that happening. So when a company like ROH is bought by AEW in 2022, or when AAA is bought by WWE in 2025, it’s pretty crazy to me. Now what will the future hold for AAA and lucha libre in Mexico? I’m not sure and that worries me. If you’ve followed WWE’s history with working with other companies, you know the track record they have. They’re not working with another wrestling company just to have a great mutual relationship, they want to get something out of it which is usually just taking over the company. TNA and NOAH could be on deck at some point if WWE have their way. As for AAA, their product isn’t for me but every now and then there will be a main event match that is must see, although it’s been a few years since then. Coming from someone who knows little about the current lucha libre scene, here is what I think WWE will do. They’ll use AAA to help them get attention in Mexico since that is a market WWE has chased for years. They want to get attention in Mexico, despite several failed attempts at making big Latino stars. If it works, it may get worse for AAA’s future as they will most likely just become a company made of wrestlers that will eventually just be pulled to NXT and/or the main roster. If it doesn’t work? Well I don’t know how long AAA will last, and that’s pretty sad just considering the long history AAA has in professional wrestling. Regardless if you watch them right now or not, it’s a history that shouldn’t be forgotten about, but now that it’s in the hands of WWE that could very well happen. All in all, I’m very skeptical on the future of WWE, AAA, and wrestling in Mexico as a whole. By the way, if you don’t think the WWE/AAA relationship has nothing to do with CMLL/AEW’s relationship that seems to be booming right now with future collab shows coming in June, then you’re out of your freaking mind. (WWE also announced their show with AAA coming a few days before CMLL/AEW’s shows will be happening too, just a conicidence I’m sure right?)

## 3. Bayley left off Mania is disgusting

![Image 93](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2945-1.jpg?w=1024)
On the countdown show on Saturday, there was an angle where Bayley was attacked backstage and it was announced that she will not be at Wrestlemania on Sunday. While we will get to the mystery partner on Night 2 later, I do think it’s absurd that Bayley is left off Wrestlemania. Regardless of the reasons or the story behind why, I don’t see why you’d take her off of Mania and announce you’re taking her off the day before she’s supposed to wrestle. I haven’t liked much of Bayley since Wrestlemania last year but I do respect how hard she works and this is how WWE treats someone like Bayley, a cornerstone of their women’s division for the past decade? It’s not a great look and it’s a one of the several stains on WWE this whole Mania week.

## 4. Gunther gets punked out

![Image 94](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2946-1.jpg?w=305)
One of the most misused world title runs ever ends with a the champ tapping to his own submission move by a wrestler 10 times worse than he is. Jey Uso made Gunther tap to open Night 1 in a pretty okay match with a horrible ending. Defend it all you want, I can’t find a good reason for it. Just have Jey win with his actual finisher or a roll up, don’t make your champ look like a total geek tapping out to the guy who dances in the crowd. This whole Jey Uso experiment continues to flounder on through the summer unfortunately. As for Gunther, I have no idea what the future is for him, maybe take some time off and let them figure it out.

## 5. Night 1 Main Event Saved The Show

![Image 95](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2947-1.jpg?w=640)
The undercard of Night 1 wasn’t necessarily bad, there was just nothing happening. Up until the main event, Night 1 was just a nothing show with maybe one match that was “okay” or “good” but nothing WrestleMania level…until the last match. Seth Rollins, Roman Reigns and CM Punk did more than expected and provided a very good main event triple threat match even if it did have some added drama that isn’t for everyone. The match told a very good story with a surprising ending which has people talking, not much more you could want from your Mania main event. Rollins got the shocking win with the assist from Paul Heyman, while Roman was the one to take the loss and Punk despite the loss has now main evented Wrestlemania and no one can take that from him. The triple threat undoubtedly saved the show from being a complete disaster.

## 6. Bianca/Iyo/Rhea steal the entire weekend

![Image 96](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2979-1.jpg?w=686)
Night 2 of Wrestlemania kicked off with an instant classic, and one of the best opening matches to a Wrestlemania ever. Iyo Sky, Bianca Belair and Rhea Ripley tore the house down with a great triple threat match with better action than almost all of Night 1 combined. Some people call these three women the Big 3, and this match is proof why. Iyo, Bianca and Rhea are the present and future of the women’s division and they should be treated like it after having matches like this.

## 7. Dirty Dom is a future star

![Image 97](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2980-1.jpg?w=686)
The 4 way for the IC title surprised me as I was worried the match would be too dramatic with Dom and Finn arguing. Instead, Dom and Finn just wanted to win the match and the title and fought each other instead of arguing and making faces at each other. Penta and Bron were also great in the match, but the talking point coming out of this match is Dominik and how much the crowd loved him. It’s clear to see now that people legit love this guy and WWE needs to capitalize on it NOW. Will they? That remains to be seen, but I’d love to see Dom as a Eddie Guerrero-ish babyface soon. Dom’s always had this in him, the booking just needed to treat him like a star instead of a child or someone’s lackey…maybe now that can finally happen with Dom winning the IC title.

## 8. Joe Hendry??????

![Image 98](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2981-1.jpg?w=650)
Randy Orton’s opponent at Wrestlemania was left up in the air after Kevin Owens announced he needed surgery. There were many names thrown out there, but it was hard to come up with a name personally. In the end, I predicted a Rusev return, but boy was I wrong. Whoever were the ones to predict Joe Hendry (the current TNA World Champion), all 10 of you were correct! I like Joe Hendry from a distance, and I thought this SAY HIS NAME stuff was funny, but it’s not something to be taken as a serious or main event role like he is TNA, let alone against a top name in WWE. I guess the match and everything was okay for what it was, but it definitely didn’t do anything for me. I’m not sure if this did anything for Hendry or TNA and I think the Hendry gimmick itself has kind of ran its course but he did get a reaction last night so what do I know. All I know is once Hendry came out, the momentum of Night 2 died and they struggled to get that momentum back the rest of the night.

## 9. The Karrion Kross Saga

![Image 99](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2982.jpg?w=640)
I was initially going to tie Karrion Kross into the last point I made about Joe Hendry because why in the world is Karrion Kross involved in anything on this Wrestlemania when other talent were left off the show entirely? I’ve always liked Kross since he was Killer Kross in Impact Wrestling, but lately you can tell his matches just aren’t as good as his promos and character work and you need all 3 to be good if you’re going to succeed (least in theory, you could also be Jey Uso). The reason Kross gets his own paragraph here isn’t for anything he did on the actual show itself, but on the Wrestlemania Recap show on YouTube that uploaded tomorrow. If you haven’t seen it, Kross started the promo off talking about Logan Paul and how all Paul had to do to be on Wrestlemania was be a Youtuber while Kross has busted his behind on the indies for years just to get in WWE, and then get released, just to come back and be in a similar spot he was in before he was released. Kross then aired his frustations about how he’s been treated in the company, with his wife Scarlett trying to console him as Kross continues what is more of a rant it seems than an actual promo. Kross then drops some curse words that I will not repeat and the two leave the room leaving Sam Roberts and Megan Morant unsure what to do. Now here’s the deal, people are going to say this is a shoot, a work, a worked shoot (brother?) or whatever they’re going to say. Clearly, this was something WWE knew was coming because why upload something that was recorded the night before unedited if you didn’t think that was coming. Now, did WWE know everything Kross was going to say? Maybe not, but I will say it was a hell of a promo nonetheless and it might be the best thing Kross has done in wrestling. Now, will this go anywhere? Is a storyline coming? Kross did mention his contract status at the very end of the promo, so I have no idea. If this is a planned story, then I hope something good comes from it because again I do think Kross has potential even if the matches are lackluster. If it was me, I’d have Kross lead a faction so he can do all the talking and none of the wrestling…now yes they did that before and WWE fired the whole group but look that’s not my problem. I just hope Kross gets treated better in the future and good on him for being able to get that off his chest.

## 10. The Man is back……I guess….

![Image 100](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2983.jpg?w=1024)
Let me start off by saying Becky Lynch is probably favorite female wrestler of all time, depending on the day I could flip to either her or Mercedes Mone…or maybe some Joshi wrestlers…but you get the idea that I love Becky Lynch. While she was away, I read her book and thought it was a great read. Believe me when I say I am always happy to see Becky Lynch come back and get in the ring…but this time I wasn’t so happy to see The Man. Becky Lynch returned last night to team with Lyra Valkyria and win the women’s tag team titles. Sure it was a big moment…for Becky and Lyra fans. From the moment Bayley was “attacked” and the speculation grew about Becky taking her place, it all gave me bad memories from Summerslam 2021. If you know you know, Becky Lynch took Sasha Bank’s place, turned heel and beat Bianca Belair for her title in like 20 to 30 seconds. It was not great, and I don’t think this run is going to be that great either. Will Becky and Lyra have fun tag matches? Sure. Could a heel Becky feuding with Lyra in a few months be fun and help Lyra get over, which is probably something Becky would want to do? Yes to all of those. However, I wasn’t crazy about Becky’s last heel run and there’s already several heel runs in wrestling I’m not crazy about (more on that in a second). Plus, was this the right spot for a Becky return? You couldn’t do this match some time after Mania and let Bayley have her Mania match she’s earned? I don’t know, there’s a lot of things about this Becky run that are off putting to me and I have no idea if that will change any time soon. I will say that someone like Becky is always needed on the roster, regardless if I don’t like the booking or not.

## 11. John Cena’s future

![Image 101](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2984-1.jpg?w=1024)
Last night, a record was broken. John Cena defeated Cody Rhodes to win his 17th world title…now what? Yes, some of the heel Cena stuff I like. I like that he came out with no colors or graphics in his entrance…I’ve liked most of the promos he’s cut so far…but then the bell rings. We all knew John Cena wasn’t as good in the ring as he used to be, but we were fine with it because of the spots on the cards John was on. Now, he’s in the main event of the wrestling doing 80s heel work on Cody Rhodes. It doesn’t work, Cena’s clearly washed sadly and he also isn’t used to working heel. Not to mention the poor finish to the main event that featured Travis Scott. If the match Cena had with Cody Rhodes is the kind of match he’s going to have with possible names like Randy Orton and CM Punk…I’m not sure if I’m going to be into this Cena heel run much longer. I wasn’t old enough to remember Stone Cold’s heel run and how it affected business…but I think I may get an idea soon because…

## 12. Wrestlemania 41 was very average overall, and so has WWE’s product this year so far

![Image 102](https://austinonrasslin.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/img_2985-1.jpg?w=840)
Let’s face it, WWE is on a down year right now…yes I know it’s only April but aside from a handful of great matches and moments, WWE’s product this year has had a lot to be desired. Look at what they’re doing with the John Cena heel run people have fantasy booked for a decade plus, it’s not bad by any means but I do think it could be better. Plus, now you just derailed a white hot Cody Rhodes for an aging John Cena heel run who has Travis Scott helping him to win a world title. This year’s Wrestlemania didn’t have the hype of the past two Wrestlemanias and it didn’t have the quality of the past two Wrestlemanias. I’ve tried my best to give ole Papa Haitch the benefit of the doubt, but it’s starting to seem like a break from this product might be in the cards for me…but of course it’s wrestling and we can’t stay away from it too long…even WWE. I do hope WWE can turn things around, but I think it’s going to take a drastic show or main event match for them to finally pivot and make changes.
